pattern.title: English Grammar
pattern.description: Core grammar rules tested in placements.

questions.questionText: She ____ in Coimbatore since 2019.
questions.explanation: Since + a point in time, for a state that began in the past and continues now, takes the present perfect: has lived.

questions.questionText: The train ____ before we reached the platform.
questions.explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one uses the past perfect. Leaving happened before reaching, so: had left.

questions.questionText: Water ____ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts and universal truths use the simple present: boils.

questions.questionText: I ____ my homework when the lights went out.
questions.explanation: A longer ongoing past action interrupted by a shorter one (went out, simple past) takes the past continuous: was doing.

questions.questionText: By next June, Ravi ____ his degree.
questions.explanation: 'By + a future time' signals an action finished before that time: future perfect, will have completed.

questions.questionText: Look! The children ____ in the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' points to an action happening right now: present continuous, are playing.

questions.questionText: He ____ to Madurai last Sunday.
questions.explanation: A finished time marker (last Sunday) requires the simple past: went.

questions.questionText: My father ____ the newspaper every morning.
questions.explanation: 'Every morning' shows a habit: simple present, reads.

questions.questionText: They ____ their lunch yet.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' in a negative sentence goes with the present perfect: have not finished. (Also 'did not finished' is wrong: after did not, the verb stays in base form.)

questions.questionText: Neha ____ sushi in her life.
questions.explanation: 'In her life' covers time up to now, so the present perfect is used: has never eaten.

questions.questionText: No sooner had he entered the room than the phone ____.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had + V3 ... than' is followed by the simple past: rang.
questions.shortcut: No sooner had ... than + simple past.

questions.questionText: Hardly had the match begun when it ____ to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had + V3 ... when' is followed by the simple past: started.

questions.questionText: I ____ for two hours before the manager called me in for the interview.
questions.explanation: A continuous action lasting up to a past moment ('before the manager called') takes the past perfect continuous: had been waiting.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: I was knowing him since childhood.
I am knowing him since childhood.
I have known him since childhood.

questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in continuous tenses. Since + point in time needs the present perfect: have known.

questions.questionText: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ____.
questions.explanation: The film started before we arrived (a past moment), so the earlier action uses the past perfect.

questions.questionText: I will call you as soon as I ____ home.
questions.explanation: In time clauses (as soon as, when, after, before, until) the future is expressed by the simple present, not will: reach.

questions.questionText: Ravi ____ in Chennai for ten years before he moved to Pune.
questions.explanation: 'Before he moved' fixes a past reference point; a state lasting up to it takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.questionText: Tomorrow at this time, we ____ in the exam hall.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future moment takes the future continuous: will be sitting.

questions.questionText: The manager ____ the report since morning but has not finished it.
questions.explanation: 'Since morning' plus an action still unfinished takes the present perfect continuous: has been preparing.

questions.questionText: While the teacher ____ the lesson, two students were chatting.
questions.explanation: Two simultaneous past actions in progress take the past continuous in both clauses: was explaining / were chatting.

questions.questionText: I ____ you last week, but you were out.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' is a finished time, so the simple past is required: called.

questions.questionText: The earthquake occurred while the villagers ____.
questions.explanation: 'While' with a past action in progress takes the past continuous: were sleeping.

questions.questionText: I will phone you after the meeting ____.
questions.explanation: In an 'after' time clause the future is shown by the simple present: ends.

questions.questionText: It is high time you ____ preparing for the exam.
questions.explanation: 'It is (high) time + subject' is followed by the simple past (unreal present urgency): started.

questions.questionText: Ravi is not at home; he ____ to the market.
questions.explanation: 'Has gone' means he is still there; 'has been' means he went and came back. He is not at home, so: has gone.

questions.questionText: My cousin ____ in Dubai for five years now.
questions.explanation: 'For five years now' shows an activity continuing up to the present: present perfect continuous, has been working.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I have been seeing him yesterday.

questions.explanation: A definite finished time (yesterday) cannot be used with the present perfect; use the simple past: saw.

questions.questionText: By the time you read this letter, I ____ for Mumbai.
questions.explanation: 'By the time' + a future moment shows completion before it: future perfect, will have left.

questions.questionText: This is the first time I ____ a motorbike.
questions.explanation: 'This is the first time' takes the present perfect: have ridden.
questions.shortcut: This is the first time + present perfect.

questions.questionText: He ____ the exam three times before he finally passed it.
questions.explanation: The failures happened before the later past event (passed), so the past perfect is used: had failed.

questions.questionText: By next April, Mrs Iyer ____ in this school for twenty years.
questions.explanation: 'By + future time' with duration ('for twenty years') takes the future perfect continuous: will have been teaching.

questions.questionText: Since the project began, the team ____ three major problems.
questions.explanation: 'Since + past event' with an unfinished period up to now takes the present perfect: has faced.

questions.questionText: She ____ the piano for years, so she plays very well.
questions.explanation: A long activity continuing up to now, with 'for years', takes the present perfect continuous: has been playing.

questions.questionText: She is ____ honest girl.
questions.explanation: Honest begins with a vowel SOUND (silent h), so 'an' is used.

questions.questionText: He bought ____ umbrella yesterday.
questions.explanation: Umbrella begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article is 'an'.

questions.questionText: She is studying at ____ university in Pune.
questions.explanation: University begins with the consonant sound /j/, so 'a' is used.

questions.questionText: ____ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: Unique objects such as the sun, moon and earth take the definite article.

questions.questionText: ____ Ganga is considered a holy river in India.
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take 'the'.

questions.questionText: Mount Everest is ____ highest peak in the world.
questions.explanation: A superlative adjective takes 'the': the highest.

questions.questionText: He plays ____ guitar very well.
questions.explanation: With musical instruments, 'play' takes 'the': play the guitar.

questions.questionText: ____ gold is a precious metal.
questions.explanation: Material nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.questionText: She wears ____ expensive watch.
questions.explanation: Expensive starts with a vowel sound, and the watch is introduced for the first time, so 'an'.

questions.questionText: I saw a film yesterday. ____ film was very entertaining.
questions.explanation: A noun already mentioned takes 'the' on second mention.

questions.questionText: It took me ____ hour to reach the station.
questions.explanation: Hour has a silent h and starts with a vowel sound, so 'an'.

questions.questionText: ____ Mahatma Gandhi was born in Porbandar.
questions.explanation: Names of persons take no article.
questions.shortcut: Proper name of a person = no article.

questions.questionText: He is ____ best player in the team.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'best' needs the definite article.

questions.questionText: Tamil is ____ ancient language.
questions.explanation: Ancient begins with a vowel sound, and Tamil is described by a general adjective phrase, so 'an'.

questions.questionText: She reads ____ Times of India every morning.
questions.explanation: Names of newspapers take 'the'.

questions.questionText: Mr Sharma is ____ engineer.
questions.explanation: Engineer begins with a vowel sound, and a profession is described with an indefinite article.

questions.questionText: My brother is ____ M.B.A. from IIM Ahmedabad.
questions.explanation: M is pronounced 'em', a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.
questions.shortcut: Letters like F, H, L, M, N, R, S, X start with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: Rahul is ____ one-eyed man.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so 'a' is used.

questions.questionText: She goes to ____ school at 8 a.m.
questions.explanation: When school is visited for its primary purpose (studying), no article is used.
questions.shortcut: Institution used for its purpose = no article.

questions.questionText: The mother went to ____ school to meet the principal.
questions.explanation: Here the school is visited as a building for a different purpose, so 'the' is used.

questions.questionText: She travels to office by ____ bus.
questions.explanation: Means of transport after 'by' takes no article: by bus, by train.

questions.questionText: He is ____ European by birth.
questions.explanation: European begins with the consonant sound /j/, so 'a' is used.

questions.questionText: ____ Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world.
questions.explanation: Names of mountain ranges take 'the'.
questions.shortcut: Ranges and plural island groups take the.

questions.questionText: She had ____ breakfast at 7 a.m.
questions.explanation: Names of meals used in general take no article.

questions.questionText: He is ____ MLA from Tamil Nadu.
questions.explanation: MLA is pronounced 'em-el-ay', beginning with a vowel sound, so 'an'.
questions.shortcut: Initialisms: go by the first letter's sound.

questions.questionText: ____ poor are often neglected by society.
questions.explanation: 'The' with an adjective denotes a whole class of people: the poor.

questions.questionText: They travelled to ____ Maldives last summer.
questions.explanation: Names of island groups take 'the': the Maldives.

questions.questionText: She has ____ MBBS degree but wants to do an MD.
questions.explanation: MBBS begins with 'em', a vowel sound, so 'an'.

questions.questionText: We had ____ wonderful breakfast at the hotel.
questions.explanation: When an adjective qualifies a meal and it is a particular instance, 'a' is used.

questions.questionText: Both of ____ boys passed the test.
questions.explanation: After 'both of', a definite plural noun requires 'the'.

questions.questionText: He is ____ more intelligent of the two brothers.
questions.explanation: In a comparison between two, the comparative takes 'the': the more intelligent of the two.

questions.questionText: He is a man of ____ word.
questions.explanation: In the idiom 'a man of his word' the possessive his is required.

questions.questionText: The meeting is scheduled ____ 10 a.m.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with exact clock times.

questions.questionText: She was born ____ 12 March 1999.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with specific dates and days.

questions.questionText: We usually go to Ooty ____ summer.
questions.explanation: 'In' is used with months, seasons and years.

questions.questionText: He has been working here ____ 2018.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time at which a continuing action began.

questions.questionText: She has been waiting ____ two hours.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.questionText: The book is ____ the table.
questions.explanation: 'On' shows a surface contact position.

questions.questionText: She is jealous ____ her colleague's success.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'jealous' is followed by 'of': jealous of her colleague's success.

questions.questionText: He is addicted ____ online games.
questions.explanation: 'Addicted' is followed by 'to'.

questions.questionText: She is afraid ____ spiders.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'afraid' is always followed by 'of': afraid of spiders.

questions.questionText: This road leads ____ the railway station.
questions.explanation: 'Lead' takes 'to' for a destination.

questions.questionText: The boy is fond ____ chocolates.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'fond' is always followed by 'of': fond of chocolates.

questions.questionText: She is married ____ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'married' is followed by 'to' before the spouse: married to a doctor.

questions.questionText: The shop remains closed ____ Sundays.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with days of the week.

questions.questionText: I prefer tea ____ coffee.
questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes 'to', not 'than', for comparison: prefer tea to coffee.

questions.questionText: The thief jumped ____ the wall and ran away.
questions.explanation: 'Over' shows movement across and beyond an obstacle.

questions.questionText: I have no objection ____ your plan.
questions.explanation: The noun 'objection' is followed by the preposition 'to': objection to your plan.

questions.questionText: The teacher congratulated him ____ his success.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' takes 'on' with the achievement.

questions.questionText: He has been suffering ____ fever since Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Suffer' takes 'from' with an illness.

questions.questionText: The accused was charged ____ murder.
questions.explanation: 'Charge' takes 'with' for the offence alleged.

questions.questionText: He insisted ____ paying the bill.
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' is followed by 'on' and then a gerund: insist on paying.

questions.questionText: I am looking forward ____ meeting you.
questions.explanation: 'Look forward' takes 'to'; 'to' is a preposition so a gerund follows.

questions.questionText: The project must be completed ____ Friday, not later.
questions.explanation: 'By' means not later than a deadline.

questions.questionText: He stayed in the library ____ 8 p.m. and then left.
questions.explanation: 'Until' shows continuing action up to a time.

questions.questionText: The Taj Mahal is ____ the banks of the Yamuna.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with banks of a river.

questions.questionText: He sat ____ his two friends on the bench.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons or things, here sitting with one at each side.

questions.questionText: The sweets were distributed ____ the children.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two persons.

questions.questionText: She is senior ____ me by two years.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to', not 'than'.

questions.questionText: The committee is composed ____ ten members.
questions.explanation: The participle 'composed' is followed by 'of': composed of ten members.

questions.questionText: This soap differs ____ the one I used earlier in its fragrance.
questions.explanation: The verb 'differ' is followed by 'from': differs from the one used earlier.

questions.questionText: The new rule is applicable ____ all employees.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'applicable' is followed by 'to': applicable to all employees.

questions.questionText: He apologised ____ the delay to the customer.
questions.explanation: 'Apologise' takes 'for' with the fault.

questions.questionText: The passengers got ____ the bus at Salem.
questions.explanation: 'Get off' is used with buses, trains and planes.
questions.shortcut: bus/train: get on/off; car: get in/out.

questions.questionText: She was angry ____ me for being late.
questions.explanation: 'Angry' takes 'with' before a person.

questions.questionText: He is angry ____ the delay in delivery.
questions.explanation: 'Angry' takes 'at' before a thing or situation.

questions.questionText: The box of mangoes ____ on the table.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'box'; 'of mangoes' does not change it. Singular subject takes 'is'.
questions.shortcut: Ignore the phrase between subject and verb.

questions.questionText: Each of the students ____ a separate locker.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb: has.

questions.questionText: Neither of the two answers ____ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' used with 'of' is treated as singular: is.

questions.questionText: Ravi and Karthik ____ going to the match tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s, such as mathematics, are singular.

questions.questionText: The news about the strike ____ shocking.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and singular: was.

questions.questionText: One of my cousins ____ in Dubai.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'one', singular, so 'lives'.
questions.shortcut: One of + plural noun = singular verb.

questions.questionText: Where ____ my glasses?
questions.explanation: 'Glasses' (spectacles) is a plural noun: are.

questions.questionText: Everyone in the room ____ clapping.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular: was.

questions.questionText: The poet and the painter ____ great friends.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: There ____ many reasons for his failure.
questions.explanation: In a 'there' sentence the verb agrees with the real subject 'reasons' (plural): are.
questions.shortcut: There is/are: check the noun after it.

questions.questionText: Bread and butter ____ my usual breakfast.
questions.explanation: Two nouns forming one idea are treated as a single unit: Bread and butter is.
questions.shortcut: One idea joined by and = singular.

questions.questionText: Either the manager or his assistants ____ responsible for the error.
questions.explanation: With either...or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'assistants' (plural): are.

questions.questionText: Neither the players nor the coach ____ happy with the result.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'coach' (singular); the past context gives was.

questions.questionText: The police ____ arrested the suspect last night.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb: have.

questions.questionText: Fifty rupees ____ too much for this pen.
questions.explanation: A sum of money treated as a single amount takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The number of vacancies ____ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: A number of candidates ____ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb: are.

questions.questionText: The Lok Sabha ____ adjourned till Monday.
questions.explanation: The name of a single body such as the Lok Sabha is treated as singular, so the past singular 'was' is used.

questions.questionText: The teacher, along with her students, ____ visiting the museum.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not make the subject plural; the subject 'teacher' is singular: is.
questions.shortcut: along with / as well as / with = ignore.

questions.questionText: Not only the principal but also the teachers ____ present.
questions.explanation: With not only...but also, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teachers': were.

questions.questionText: Two-thirds of the land ____ under cultivation.
questions.explanation: With fractions, agreement follows the noun after 'of'; 'land' is singular: is.

questions.questionText: Two-thirds of the apples ____ rotten.
questions.explanation: With fractions, agreement follows the noun after 'of'; 'apples' is plural: are.

questions.questionText: Who ____ the author of this novel?
questions.explanation: 'Who' asking about one person takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The scholar and the poet ____ both attended the function.
questions.explanation: 'Both' together with two subjects joined by 'and' shows plural: have.

questions.questionText: Ten kilometres ____ a long distance to walk in an hour.
questions.explanation: A distance considered as one unit takes a singular verb: is.

questions.questionText: The Arabian Nights ____ a collection of stories.
questions.explanation: The title of a single work is singular: is.

questions.questionText: The jury ____ divided in their opinions.
questions.explanation: When the members act individually, a collective noun takes a plural verb: were.

questions.questionText: A pair of scissors ____ on the table.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'pair', which is singular: is.

questions.questionText: My friend as well as my brothers ____ invited to the wedding.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the first subject 'friend' (singular) when 'as well as' is used: was.
questions.shortcut: A as well as B: agree with A.

questions.questionText: The secretary and treasurer ____ resigned.
questions.explanation: With one article before both nouns, both titles refer to one person, so the verb is singular: has.

questions.questionText: There ____ two books and a pen on the desk.
questions.explanation: In a 'there' sentence the verb agrees with the first noun that follows, 'two books' (plural): are.

questions.questionText: It is I who ____ responsible for this decision.
questions.explanation: In a relative clause the verb agrees with the antecedent 'I': am.
questions.shortcut: who takes the person of its antecedent.

questions.questionText: Many a student ____ failed in this paper.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb: has.

questions.questionText: The prize was shared between Anita and ____.
questions.explanation: After a preposition (between), the object form 'me' is used.

questions.questionText: Rahul and ____ went to the market.
questions.explanation: As part of the subject, the subject form 'I' is needed.

questions.questionText: She blamed ____ for the accident.
questions.explanation: The subject and object are the same person, so a reflexive pronoun is needed: herself.
questions.shortcut: Same person doing and receiving = reflexive.

questions.questionText: The book is not mine; it is ____.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone completes the sentence: hers.
questions.shortcut: Possessive pronoun has no noun after it.

questions.questionText: This is ____ umbrella, not yours.
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective is followed by a noun: my umbrella.

questions.questionText: The old man lost ____ way in the forest.
questions.explanation: The pronoun must match the singular male subject 'old man': his.

questions.questionText: Kavya and Divya completed ____ projects before the deadline.
questions.explanation: The plural subject takes the plural possessive: their.

questions.questionText: This is the girl ____ won the first prize.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'won'. Persons take who.

questions.questionText: The watch ____ I bought yesterday has stopped.
questions.explanation: The antecedent is a thing, so the relative pronoun 'which' is used; who/whom are for persons.

questions.questionText: They enjoyed ____ at the festival.
questions.explanation: The subject and object are the same, so the reflexive 'themselves' is used.

questions.questionText: We should respect ____ elders.
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective is needed before the noun 'elders': our.

questions.questionText: Seema and Reena are friends; ____ love each other.
questions.explanation: A plural subject needed for two girls: they.

questions.questionText: Which of these two bags is ____?
questions.explanation: A standalone possessive pronoun is needed here: yours.

questions.questionText: It was ____ who called you yesterday.
questions.explanation: After 'it was' the subject form is used with a following relative clause: he.

questions.questionText: Each of the boys has finished ____ homework.
questions.explanation: 'Each of the boys' is singular and refers to male persons: his.

questions.questionText: The company has changed ____ policy on refunds.
questions.explanation: A company as one unit is referred to with 'its'.

questions.questionText: He did all the work by ____ without any help.
questions.explanation: 'By himself' means alone; the reflexive follows the preposition when it refers back to the subject.

questions.questionText: Between you and ____, the plan will not work.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition and takes the object form: me.

questions.questionText: She is not as intelligent as ____ am.
questions.explanation: The verb 'am' needs a subject, so the subject form I is used.

questions.questionText: Do you know ____ is waiting outside?
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'is waiting', so the subject form is used.

questions.questionText: To ____ did you give the keys?
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to', the object form 'whom' is used.

questions.questionText: The man ____ car was stolen reported to the police.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun shows possession of the car, so 'whose'.

questions.questionText: He is the man to ____ I gave the money.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to', the object form 'whom' is used.

questions.questionText: She prepared the dinner ____.
questions.explanation: Used for emphasis, the reflexive 'herself' follows the noun or the verb phrase.

questions.questionText: The lion hurt ____ while trying to escape the cage.
questions.explanation: A lion as an animal is referred to as 'it', and since the subject and object are the same, 'itself' is required.

questions.questionText: The teacher told Meena and ____ to stay back.
questions.explanation: 'Told' takes an object, so the object form 'me' is needed.

questions.questionText: Let you and ____ finish the work first.
questions.explanation: 'Let' takes an object form: let you and me.

questions.questionText: Only the two of ____ know the password.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'of', the object form is used: us.

questions.questionText: The students ____ passed the test were awarded certificates.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to persons and is the subject of 'passed': who.

questions.questionText: The old woman ____ I met yesterday is my neighbour.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of 'met' and refers to a person: whom.

questions.questionText: The climate of Ooty is cooler than ____ of Chennai.
questions.explanation: 'That' stands for the singular noun 'climate' to avoid repetition.

questions.questionText: Hari as well as ____ was selected for the camp.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject of 'was selected', so the subject form: I.

questions.questionText: The leaves of this plant are bigger than ____ of that plant.
questions.explanation: 'Those' stands for the plural noun 'leaves' to avoid repetition.

questions.questionText: He worked hard, ____ he failed the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' shows contrast between effort and failure.

questions.questionText: It was raining heavily, ____ we stayed indoors.
questions.explanation: 'So' shows result: rain caused them to stay in.

questions.questionText: He stayed at home ____ he was unwell.
questions.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for staying at home.

questions.questionText: ____ he was tired, he finished the report.
questions.explanation: 'Although' shows concession: tired, yet finished.

questions.questionText: Hurry up, ____ you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: 'Or' gives the consequence of not hurrying.

questions.questionText: Study hard, ____ you will pass.
questions.explanation: 'And' joins a command with a favourable result.

questions.questionText: Neither the manager ____ the clerk was present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor'.

questions.questionText: Either you apologise ____ you leave the room.
questions.explanation: 'Either' pairs with 'or'.

questions.questionText: I will wait here ____ you return.
questions.explanation: 'Until' shows the time up to which waiting continues.

questions.questionText: She is poor ____ honest.
questions.explanation: 'But' joins two contrasting qualities.

questions.questionText: ____ it was cold, he went out without a sweater.
questions.explanation: 'Though' expresses concession.

questions.questionText: Whether he comes ____ not, we will start the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'Whether' pairs with 'or'.

questions.questionText: Please call me ____ you reach home.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' marks the time immediately after an event.

questions.questionText: You will not pass ____ you study regularly.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'; a negative main clause with 'unless' is correct.

questions.questionText: Not only did she sing well, ____ she also danced beautifully.
questions.explanation: 'Not only ... but also' is a correlative pair.

questions.questionText: Hardly had he reached the station ____ the train left.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' pairs with 'when'.

questions.questionText: No sooner did the bell ring ____ the students rushed out.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'.

questions.questionText: Scarcely had she sat down ____ the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely' pairs with 'when'.

questions.questionText: He speaks ____ he were the manager.
questions.explanation: 'As if' compares the behaviour with an imagined situation.

questions.questionText: He ran fast ____ he could catch the bus.
questions.explanation: 'So that' expresses purpose.

questions.questionText: He was ____ tired that he could not walk.
questions.explanation: 'So ... that' expresses result with an adjective.

questions.questionText: It was ____ a hot day that nobody went out.
questions.explanation: 'Such a + adjective + noun ... that' expresses result.

questions.questionText: The shop was closed; ____, we returned home.
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' introduces a result of the previous statement.

questions.questionText: He is rich; ____, he is not happy.
questions.explanation: 'However' marks contrast with the previous clause.

questions.questionText: She is intelligent; ____, she is hardworking.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further point to the same idea.

questions.questionText: Take an umbrella; ____, you may get wet.
questions.explanation: 'Otherwise' shows the consequence of not doing the action.

questions.questionText: The doctor insisted ____ he should take rest.
questions.explanation: 'That' introduces the noun clause that follows 'insisted'.

questions.questionText: I do not know ____ he has left.
questions.explanation: 'Whether' introduces an indirect question.

questions.questionText: He left early ____ he could attend the interview.
questions.explanation: 'So that' expresses purpose.

questions.questionText: He asked me ____ I had completed the work.
questions.explanation: 'If' introduces an indirect yes/no question.

questions.questionText: He will come ____ it rains.
questions.explanation: 'Even if' means regardless of the condition.

questions.questionText: The more you practise, ____ you will perform.
questions.explanation: 'The more ... the better' is the comparative correlative.

questions.questionText: ____ the weather was bad, the match was held as planned.
questions.explanation: 'Despite the fact that' can be followed by a clause; 'despite' alone needs a noun.
questions.shortcut: despite + noun; despite the fact that + clause.

questions.questionText: She sings ____.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: beautifully.

questions.questionText: He is a ____ driver.
questions.explanation: A noun is modified by an adjective: careful driver.

questions.questionText: He is the ____ of the three brothers.
questions.explanation: For more than two, the superlative 'tallest' is used.

questions.questionText: This book is ____ than that one.
questions.explanation: 'Good' has the irregular comparative 'better'.

questions.questionText: He is ____ intelligent than his brother.
questions.explanation: The comparative of a long adjective uses 'more'.

questions.questionText: She is the ____ girl in the class.
questions.explanation: For a long adjective, the superlative is formed with 'most'.

questions.questionText: She is as ____ as her mother.
questions.explanation: In 'as ... as', the adjective is in the positive form: tall.

questions.questionText: The Ganga is the ____ river in India.
questions.explanation: Among many rivers, the superlative 'longest' is used.

questions.questionText: Mohan is ____ boy in the class.
questions.explanation: A superlative with 'in the class' is formed with 'the'.

questions.questionText: She speaks English very ____.
questions.explanation: 'Speaks' needs an adverb: fluently.

questions.questionText: There is ____ milk in the fridge.
questions.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so 'some' is used.

questions.questionText: Which of the two routes is ____?
questions.explanation: Two items compared: use the comparative.

questions.questionText: The soup tastes ____.
questions.explanation: After a linking verb such as 'taste', an adjective is used.

questions.questionText: She looked ____ at the stranger.
questions.explanation: 'Looked at' describes an action, so an adverb is needed.

questions.questionText: She felt ____ after the long journey.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb 'felt', an adjective describing the subject is used.

questions.questionText: Of the two sisters, Meena is the ____.
questions.explanation: Between two persons of a family the comparative 'elder' is used; the superlative forms are for three or more.

questions.questionText: He has ____ money left in his wallet.
questions.explanation: 'Money' is uncountable, so 'little' (hardly any) fits the negative sense.

questions.questionText: I have ____ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
questions.explanation: 'Few' has a negative sense (hardly any) and fits with 'lonely'.
questions.shortcut: few = almost none; a few = some.

questions.questionText: She has ____ friends in Chennai who will help her.
questions.explanation: 'A few' has a positive sense (some) and fits with 'help her'.

questions.questionText: He worked ____ than anyone else in the office.
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is both adjective and adverb; its comparative is 'harder'.

questions.questionText: He ran ____ to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is an adverb without -ly.

questions.questionText: She arrived ____ for the interview and was rejected.
questions.explanation: 'Late' (adverb) means after the expected time; 'lately' means recently.
questions.shortcut: late = not on time; lately = recently.

questions.questionText: The ____ of the two proposals was accepted.
questions.explanation: 'Latter' refers to the second of two; 'last' is final of many.

questions.questionText: The ____ news about the accident shocked everyone.
questions.explanation: 'Latest' means most recent.

questions.questionText: He shows ____ interest in cricket than in football.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is uncountable, so the comparative 'less' is used.

questions.questionText: This is ____ interesting book that I have ever read.
questions.explanation: A superlative takes 'the' before 'most'.

questions.questionText: We could see ____ people at the stadium than the previous year.
questions.explanation: 'People' is countable, so 'fewer' is used.

questions.questionText: She spends ____ time on social media than before.
questions.explanation: 'Time' is uncountable, so 'less' is used.

questions.questionText: This is the ____ of the two plans.
questions.explanation: With two options, the comparative 'better' is used.

questions.questionText: She ____ ever misses a class.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ever' means almost never; the adverb 'hardly' is used.

questions.questionText: He gave me ____ information about the course.
questions.explanation: 'Further' means additional; 'farther' refers to physical distance.

questions.questionText: He is a ____ boy.
questions.explanation: A compound adjective before a noun is hyphenated: well-behaved.

questions.questionText: Your answer is ____ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Absolute' is already complete and takes no degrees; the adverb 'absolutely' fits.

questions.questionText: You ____ wear a helmet while riding a two-wheeler.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a legal or strong obligation.

questions.questionText: ____ I come in, madam?
questions.explanation: 'May' is used to ask for polite permission.

questions.questionText: She ____ swim when she was five years old.
questions.explanation: 'Could' is the past of 'can' for an ability in the past.

questions.questionText: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the picnic.
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.questionText: If I were you, I ____ accept the offer.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.questionText: If water is heated to 100 degrees, it ____.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional for general truths: if + present, present.

questions.questionText: You ____ not smoke in a hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.questionText: It ____ rain this evening; the sky is cloudy.
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility.

questions.questionText: ____ you please pass the salt?
questions.explanation: 'Could' is a polite request.

questions.questionText: He ____ not come yesterday because he was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Could not' is the past of 'cannot' for inability.

questions.questionText: The students ____ submit the form by Friday.
questions.explanation: An official obligation uses 'must'.

questions.questionText: If you heat ice, it ____.
questions.explanation: A general truth takes the present simple in both clauses.

questions.questionText: If he had studied, he ____ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.shortcut: If + had pp, would have pp.

questions.questionText: It is not necessary to carry cash, so you ____ not carry it.
questions.explanation: 'Need not' expresses absence of necessity, matching the stem.

questions.questionText: He ____ be at home; his car is outside.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong logical deduction.

questions.questionText: You ____ to respect your teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Ought' is always followed by 'to' and expresses moral duty.

questions.questionText: I wish I ____ a bigger house.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' for an unreal present, the past tense is used.

questions.questionText: If I ____ rich, I would help the poor.
questions.explanation: In unreal conditions the subjunctive 'were' is used for all subjects.

questions.questionText: Unless you ____ hard, you will not succeed.
questions.explanation: After 'unless' the present simple is used for a future condition.

questions.questionText: You ____ have told me earlier; now it is too late.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + pp' expresses criticism of something not done.
questions.shortcut: should have = regret/advice in the past.

questions.questionText: She ____ have left already; the lights are off.
questions.explanation: 'Must have + pp' expresses a strong deduction about the past.

questions.questionText: I ____ get up early when I was in school.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' denotes a past habit that no longer exists.

questions.questionText: If you ____ me, I would have helped you.
questions.explanation: The result clause 'would have helped' needs the past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.questionText: I would rather ____ at home than go out.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.questionText: ____ I help you with the luggage?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I' is used for offers with the first person.

questions.questionText: If she ____ earlier, she would have caught the train.
questions.explanation: The result 'would have caught' requires the past perfect.

questions.questionText: He asked whether he ____ use my phone.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'can' changes to 'could'.

questions.questionText: I wish I ____ the exam last year.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' for an unreal past takes the past perfect.

questions.questionText: He suggested that she ____ a doctor.
questions.explanation: After 'suggest that', the base form (subjunctive) is used.

questions.questionText: He ____ be sixty; he looks very young.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot' expresses a strong impossibility.

questions.questionText: I am used to ____ up early.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' (accustomed) is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: It is time we ____ for the airport.
questions.explanation: 'It is time + subject' takes the past form of the verb.

questions.questionText: You ____ better see a doctor about that cough.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice and takes the base verb.

questions.questionText: Were I the Prime Minister, I ____ reduce taxes.
questions.explanation: Inverted second conditional 'Were I' is followed by 'would'.
